newsitem.title: GERMANY: Kohl calls for summit on how to spell in German.
newsitem.headline: Kohl calls for summit on how to spell in German.

text.p: Chancellor Helmut Kohl said on Friday he wanted to hold special top-level talks to sort out growing confusion over plans to reform German language spelling and grammar rules.

The reforms aim to standardise and simplify spelling and grammar rules, making German easier for children and foreigners to learn. But opponents say the plans will simply perplex people and destroy centuries of literary tradition.

Two regional courts have blocked the change, which has already found its way into school curricula and new editions of German dictionaries and textbooks although it will not become legally binding until 2005.

The courts have ruled that a special law is required to make such fundamental changes and not just a joint decision by local governments. But other courts have backed the reforms, saying the local governments have acted within their powers.
"What's happening at the moment is quite impossible," Kohl said in a television interview from his Austrian holiday home.

"I think it's quite unacceptable that the normal citizen... is reading something different every day, quite apart from the fact that there are economic consequences for book publishers and in many other areas," he told private broadcaster RTL.

"I'm in favour of us talking about this as soon as possible after the summer break," he said. The federal government, political parties, state premiers and local government ministers should all be included in the discussions, Kohl added.
